name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,328

entries.clue: River Test is used for manufacturing (10)

blocks.note: the Indus, the great river of Pakistan
a test = a trial

annotation.surface: A report on an English river being put to industrial use.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'River Test' look like the Hampshire trout stream; the two words have to be split, the river being a different one entirely.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the adjective for factories, plant and production lines, things used for making goods.

entries.clue: Reverse vehicle in front of a line of ships (5)

indicatorNotes.Reverse: tells you to turn the vehicle back to front
indicatorNotes.in front of: puts the reversed vehicle before the rest

blocks.note: vehicle = VAN, turned round
kept as it is
L is the standard abbreviation for line

annotation.surface: A driver backing a vehicle up to the head of a queue of ships.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A line of ships' reads as a convoy, but the definition is only 'of ships'; 'a line' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Naval means of or relating to ships and a navy.

blocks.note: high = up
a Tory is on the political right

annotation.surface: A political claim that a staunch Conservative is a person of honour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High Tory' reads as one phrase for a traditionalist Conservative; it splits into two pieces. Tory is the nickname of Britain's (and Canada's) Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: standing straight becomes morally straight, as in a citizen of good character.

indicatorNotes.in conversation: spoken aloud, so a word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: also = too, heard rather than spelt

annotation.surface: Two people who also happen to be chatting.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a couple talking together, when the talking is the signal to listen to 'too'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a pair is the number that comes after one.

blocks.note: verb sense: to set up, as proceedings or a rule
noun sense: a college or learned society

annotation.surface: An instruction to found a school.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words read as verb and object, but each is a definition on its own: one verb, one noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Institute is both a verb meaning establish and a noun for an academy.

entries.clue: Rent out fields before close of June (5)

indicatorNotes.before: puts the fields ahead of the next piece
indicatorNotes.close of: the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: leas are meadows, a poetic word for fields
last letter of June

annotation.surface: A farmer letting out pasture ahead of summer.
annotation.walkthrough: LEA (a meadow) is an old poetic word that crosswords use constantly for a field.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a landlord grants a tenancy of a flat or farm for rent.

entries.clue: Material in child’s bed not turned back (6)

indicatorNotes.turned back: tells you to write NOT backwards

blocks.note: a cot is a baby's bed (a crib)
NOT written backwards

annotation.surface: Worry over which fabric sheet goes in a baby's crib, left unfolded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not' looks like part of the instruction, but it is the word to be turned.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a fabric woven from the fluffy fibre of a plant.

indicatorNotes.contents of: the answer is inside the words that follow

blocks.note: under(COVER DO)cument

annotation.surface: A spy overstating what a secret file contains.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between 'undercover' and 'document'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to take something too far, laying it on thick.

indicatorNotes.in: puts A and D inside the show

blocks.note: an exhibition = a SHOW, opened up
A plus D, the abbreviation for day

annotation.surface: A notice describing a one-day show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outline' reads as a verb meaning summarise; the answer is a silhouette.
annotation.definitionFit: A shadow is a dark outline cast by an object.

blocks.note: verb: to mark something out for attention
noun: a flat slab of stone used for paving

annotation.walkthrough: 'Highlight' reads as a noun, the best bit; it is the verb, to pick out for notice.
annotation.surface: Pointing out a feature stone in a patio.
annotation.definitionFit: Flag means both to mark for attention and a flat paving slab.

indicatorNotes.strangely: the letters are arranged in a strange order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Someone finds a liqueur oddly stored among the teacups.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the liqueur inside the tea set; it is two letters of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a sweet French aniseed-flavoured drink.

entries.clue: A river had stripped stump in botanical garden (9)

indicatorNotes.stripped: a stripped word has lost its outer letters

blocks.note: kept as it is
R is the abbreviation for river
had = bore, as in bore a child
sTUMp without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A stream that has worn a tree stump bare in a botanic garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had' is the past of bear in the sense of giving birth or carrying: she bore/had twins.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a botanical garden given over to trees, from Latin arbor, tree.

entries.clue: Outdoor bath and barrel put back behind house (3,3)

indicatorNotes.put back: tells you to write BUTT backwards
indicatorNotes.behind: places the barrel after the house

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
a butt is a large cask; BUTT reversed

annotation.surface: Setting up a bath and an old barrel out behind the house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barrel' tempts TUB directly, which is almost right; the barrel is a BUTT, and turning it gives the second T.
annotation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a large heated bath kept outdoors.

indicatorNotes.supply: read as the adverb of supple: bent into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: Shop owners making a shortage worse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun (goods) but is the adverb from supple, pronounced SUP-lee: nimbly, so the letters bend.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: those who hold title to a shop, hotel or other property.

entries.clue: Regularly query fellow calling for immediate action (6)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: at regular intervals, so every second letter of query is kept

blocks.note: q U e R y, the even letters
a fellow = a gent

annotation.surface: A man who keeps asking questions because he needs things done now.
annotation.walkthrough: GENT is the crossword's usual fellow; 'Regularly' here keeps the second and fourth letters of query.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: pressing, needing attention right now.

entries.clue: Cooking areas close to long passageways (7)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: last letter of long
alleys are narrow passages

annotation.surface: Kitchens sited near long corridors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as near; here it means the close, the last letter, of 'long'.
annotation.definitionFit: A galley is the kitchen on a ship or aircraft.

entries.clue: The world of dancing in revues (8)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers change places across the stage, so the letters of in revues swap positions

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: The glamorous world of stage revues and their dancers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' again looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The universe is everything that exists, the whole world.

indicatorNotes.composed: the letters are put together afresh
indicatorNotes.without right: drop R, the abbreviation for right

blocks.note: the composer's name as letters
remove R (right)

annotation.surface: Antonín Dvořák writing music without any spirit in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Composed' is exactly what Dvořák did, which hides its job as the rearranging instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a clear distilled liquor from Russia and Poland.

entries.clue: Fast starts to laps ensure notable times (4)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: Laps Ensure Notable Times

annotation.surface: A runner's quick laps guaranteeing good times.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is read as speedy, fitting the running; it is the noun, a period of fasting.
annotation.definitionFit: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter.

indicatorNotes.accommodates: the city holds E inside it

blocks.note: Nice, on the Riviera
E is the abbreviation for English

annotation.surface: A French city putting up a visiting English relative.
annotation.walkthrough: Nice is the Riviera resort; the surface reads the English relative as a houseguest, when the E is simply the abbreviation for English.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a brother's or sister's daughter is one kind of relative.

entries.clue: Believe in fragment of sacred item (6)

indicatorNotes.fragment of: the answer is a piece of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of sacred and the start of item

annotation.surface: Faith placed in a splinter of a holy relic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Believe in' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Believe', and 'in' links it to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to accept a claim as true or trust a report.

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music
to mention = to refer (to)

annotation.surface: Discreetly asking for a favour.
annotation.walkthrough: P for quietly comes from piano in musical scores; 'favour' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb, to like best.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to like one option better than the others.

blocks.note: to slate or savage, as a reviewer does a flop
a metal vessel for frying or boiling

annotation.walkthrough: The two senses share a word by chance: a reviewer who pans a show has nothing to do with the kitchen.
annotation.surface: Complaining about a kitchen utensil.
annotation.definitionFit: Pan means both to criticise harshly and a cooking vessel.

blocks.note: an ad(vert) is publicity
a minister of a church

annotation.surface: A woman minister handling a parish's publicity.
annotation.walkthrough: AD is short for advertisement; a minister leads a Protestant congregation, and the clue's clergywoman is simply one who happens to be a woman.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to run the affairs of an estate, office or department.
